_comment: Registered predictions whose preconditions the harness checks before GO.
Gamma's design, and the default is the whole point: `precondition` is
`unresolved` unless someone says otherwise, and a missing field counts as
unresolved too. Silence blocks rather than passes. Any scheme that needs
someone to *declare* a dependency fails the same way the ones that failed
on 2026-07-28 did - staging by path, announcing the file, checking the
diff - because declaring is the step that gets skipped.
Resolving one is an explicit act with a name on it: set `precondition` to
`resolved`, and fill `resolvedBy` and `resolvedNote`. A false block costs
a line of typing; a false pass costs a raid.
This file cannot cover registrations that live only as prose in
FINDINGS.md. The gate counts those and says how many it did not check,
because a check that appears to cover more than it does is the failure
family this whole exercise came out of.

registrations.preconditionWas: Depends on whether item 4 also latches endToStart at the frame boundary. If it does, the alignment changes and this needs re-deriving BEFORE the raid.
registrations.resolvedNote: Not re-derived before the raid - the precondition failed, which is why this gate exists. Resolved after the fact: all three registered outcome rows fail and the answer is a fourth, the two fields moving one line apart relative to each other. 22/22 at a 0.0% coincidence baseline post-latch, 12/15 at 0.7% pre-latch.
